title: node-specs
description: The argument contract for every callable node the engine serves. This is the artifact the generated tier is derived from, so a shape change here propagates into every typed signature before anyone notices. The digest sidecar proves the bytes did not move; this schema proves the shape did not. Counts are deliberately absent -- read them from the file, with the commands in .github/inventory.json. EMITTED by scripts/gen_artifacts.py from corpus/; never edited by hand.

vocabulary.description: The closed sets the contract is written in. These are the values the runtime adapter switches on, so an unannounced addition here is a silent behaviour change rather than new documentation.

chart_kinds.description: The closed set of chart kinds a method card may declare. `none` is a member because a card that produces nothing to display must be able to say so; stretching one of the four chart kinds over that case would make the declaration a lie. method-cards.schema.json repeats the members as the enum of `chart_kind`.

precondition_gates.description: The closed set of cross-cutting gate names a method card may name as a precondition. It holds exactly the detail codes gates/registry.py PRIMITIVES resolves, so a card cannot name a check the resolver raises on; tests/test_chart_map.py asserts that this set, that registry and the enum in method-cards.schema.json are one. The per-card field is null on every card today and is populated by phase 2.2.

reseal.description: The bytes this artifact superseded, and why. The re-seal of box 2.1.15 happened IN PLACE -- same filenames, same seven sidecars, wrapper_file untouched because mcp/gateway.py and naming.py join on it -- so without this block it would leave no trace at all. The digests are the ones the sidecars carried before the re-seal; they are authored in corpus/_provenance.json rather than read from git, because .dockerignore excludes .git/ and the image build runs the generator's own suite. The same record is emitted onto node-specs.json and method-cards.json: one re-seal, one record.

fn.description: The wire name. It is the contract and cannot be renamed without breaking every saved analysis.

register.description: Null for most nodes; where present it names the field a result is registered under. `field` is itself nullable: four nodes (bsp_prior, mss_prepare_data, risk_returns_from_long, breg_set_prior) register a result under no named field, which is not the same as not registering at all.

contract_hash.description: Computed by scripts/contract_hash.py over this node's callable contract -- fn, arguments in order excluding their prose, and export. Carried with a `c2-` prefix so it can never be mistaken for a file digest, NOR for a v1 `c-` token: a v1 value came from an exporter that is not in this repository and cannot be recomputed by anything in it, surviving only in artifacts/legacy-inventory.json, so the two vocabularies are kept mutually invalid rather than merely different. It is what a Galaxy tool version pins to, so it must be a full digest and never a truncation.

cacheability.description: Four booleans, never null. A null here would be read as false by anything that tests it, which is the permissive direction and therefore the wrong one for a cache-safety flag.

export.description: Present on the three nodes that write a file. Optional by measurement, not by guess.

default.description: Any JSON value, including null. `has_default` is what distinguishes 'defaults to null' from 'has no default' -- the two are different contracts and the value alone cannot tell them apart.
